children: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD, Financials), a semiconductor company supplying processors and AI accelerators, just crossed a milestone that would have seemed out of reach a few years ago: a market value above $1 trillion.
Shares rose around 9% to 10% Monday, hitting an all-time high of nearly $614. The move has AMD up roughly 34% since the start of September and over 180% this year.
That surge is driven by real expansion in business. AMD posted second-quarter revenue of $11.54 billion, up 50% year-over-year. Data-center revenue was $6.7 billion, more than double last year's.

Wall Street, too, is signaling continued demand. Piper Sandler kept its Overweight rating and $600 price target, saying demand still outstrips supply. Stifel reiterated a Buy rating and a target of $635, citing confidence in AMD's server CPU lineup.

Another potential factor is the increasing move to AI workloads. Citi increased its 2030 worldwide CPU market prediction to $237 billion from $137 billion, citing the emergence of autonomous AI agents as a potential driver for demand for CPUs, as well as accelerators.
But the stock has already run a long way. AMD, now valued at more than $1 trillion and trading at $600 a share, requires its earnings growth to meet up with far larger expectations.
That means the next leg of the rally is less about hitting another milestone and more about whether AMD can produce the outcomes needed to justify it.

title: AMD Joins the $1 Trillion Club as AI Chip Rally Accelerates
